title: `quantile`: `nearest` by default, six methods
description: `quantile(q)` takes the `nearest` value by default (index `round(q · (n - 1))`); the other methods are `lower`, `higher`, `midpoint`, `linear` and `equiprobable`. `median` is `quantile(0.5, 'linear')`. At `q = 0.4` over 1, 2, 3, 4: nearest 2, lower 2, higher 3, midpoint 2.5, linear 2.2, equiprobable 2. NaN sorts above every number (polars-nan-order).

The position is `f = q · (n - 1)` over the non-null values; `nearest` takes index `f.round()` (halves away from zero), `linear` gives `(f - ⌊f⌋) · (hi - lo) + lo` in `f64`, `midpoint` `(lo + hi) / 2`, and equal neighbours give `lo`. For neighbours of opposite sign near the double's range `hi - lo` overflows to inf, and the result leaves the interval.

Integers go through the same kernel (`QuantileDispatcher` for every `PolarsIntegerType`), each value read `to_f64`, so the result is `Float64`. Decimals: ungrouped, the kernel runs on the scaled `Int128` values, then divides by 10^scale (two roundings); grouped, the column is first cast to `Float64` (correctly rounded). The result is `Float64` in both cases.

The result type is `moment_dtype`: integers, decimals and `Float64` give `Float64`, `Float32` (and `Float16`) keep their type, and `Date` gives `Datetime(us)`. The docs say a single quantile is f64: PL-11.

The streaming engine has no quantile reduction: ungrouped, `quantile` runs as a columnar function on the collected column and `median` through the in-memory fallback; grouped, the query falls back to the in-memory group_by. So both engines run this kernel.
reference: `quantile_disc` takes a value of the input; `quantile_cont` any double between the neighbours (`contAllowed`).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: `quantile(q, interpolation='nearest')`, methods nearest, higher, lower, midpoint, linear, equiprobable; a single quantile is one f64. Over the Int64 column 0..5 at q = 0.3: nearest 2.0, higher 2.0, lower 1.0, midpoint 1.5, linear 1.5
`median` uses linear interpolation; f64 result

notes: The examples run on an Int64 column, so the methods and the Float64 result hold for integers. They agree with the probe: nearest takes index round(0.3 · 5) = 2. The docs do not mention decimal input.
The docs at `stable` are those of Polars 2.1.0: their [source] links point at tag py-2.1.0.
